about.title: Angels Camp Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Work in and around Angels Camp often means construction along Rt 49, deliveries on Murphys Grade Road, or shifts at local shops and hospitality spots near S Main Street. When someone gets hurt on the job here, most people assume workers' compensation is the only option — and usually it is, since California treats it as the exclusive remedy against an employer regardless of fault. But when a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to the injury, a separate third-party claim may also be possible. This distinction matters because it can affect what compensation you're able to pursue beyond standard workers' comp benefits. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect injured workers in Angels Camp with an independent attorney, free of charge, who can look at the details of what happened and explain the options that actually apply to your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why Angels Camp Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding the Exclusive Remedy Rule
items.desc: California generally limits an injured worker's claim against their employer to workers' compensation, regardless of who was at fault. An attorney can help you understand whether that rule fully applies to your situation.

items.title: Spotting Third-Party Liability
items.desc: If a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker played a role in your injury, a separate claim outside workers' comp may be available. This is often overlooked without a closer look at how the injury actually happened.

items.title: Protecting Your Rights Along the Way
items.desc: California law requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and retaliation for doing so is illegal. If a third-party claim applies, it generally must be filed within two years, so timing matters.

items.question: I was hurt on a job site near Rt 49 — can I still pursue a claim outside workers' comp?
items.answer: It depends on whether someone other than your employer, like a subcontractor or equipment supplier, contributed to the injury. Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a third-party claim may exist separately. An independent attorney can review the specifics of your Angels Camp incident and let you know.

items.question: How long do I have to report a workplace injury in California?
items.answer: You generally need to notify your employer within 30 days of the injury to preserve your workers' compensation rights. Waiting too long can complicate your claim, so it's best to report as soon as possible. If a third-party claim also applies, that carries its own two-year deadline.

items.question: Can my employer retaliate against me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: No, California law prohibits retaliation against employees who report workplace injuries or file workers' comp claims. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an independent attorney can help you understand your options. This protection applies whether you work in Angels Camp or anywhere else in the state.
